hypotheses.mechanism: A live FFI/runtime resource reference carries lifetime identity in addition to a reusable storage slot or backend index.
hypotheses.expected: After close/drop and slot reuse, stale references fail closed rather than resolving to the new resource.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: A raw reusable integer index is sufficient because another runtime layer always prevents stale reuse.
hypotheses.falsifier: Production Ubuntu ClayCode runtime passes exhaustive and fuzzed close/reopen/stale-use tests with raw reusable integer handles and no hidden lifetime guard.
hypotheses.next_test: Implement two runtime ABI arms: generation/lifetime-checked table and backend-native opaque handle; compare stale-use safety, false rejection, latency and recovery.

hypotheses.mechanism: Program semantic identity, capability-grant identity, physical resource-instance identity and handle-lifetime identity remain separate dimensions.
hypotheses.expected: Recreating the same resource type/name in the same slot creates a new live instance/lifetime and does not revive old authority-bearing references.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Semantic resource type plus capability identity uniquely determines the live resource instance.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cross-backend replay demonstrates safe exact identity/recovery without a distinct resource-instance/lifetime identity.
hypotheses.next_test: Persist/recover descriptors while forcing process/file/socket handle reuse and verify reacquisition creates fresh lifetime identity.

hypotheses.mechanism: The stale-handle requirement can be implemented in typed Runtime ABI/FFI metadata and broker checks without adding a new ClayCode core syntax primitive.
hypotheses.expected: Existing typed resource/capability forms lower to a lifetime-safe host adapter with no semantic escape hatch.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Current ClayCode cannot express ownership/borrowing/drop/reacquisition semantics without a core language addition.
hypotheses.falsifier: A minimized real application or FRANK component cannot be safely lowered through existing typed forms even with an explicit runtime resource adapter.
hypotheses.next_test: Compile a grammar-conformant resource fixture end-to-end once the production frontend chain is available.
